reason: Both are prescription drug companies, but they sell different products in different ways. Akebia is a brand-owner biopharma focused on kidney disease. It sells a phosphate binder and an oral iron drug through a nephrology sales force to dialysis organizations, and it is developing a Phase 3 candidate. Elite is a generic and controlled-release manufacturer. It makes niche generics and abuse-deterrent opioids at its Northvale, NJ facility, and it does contract manufacturing and licensing. There is no product overlap: renal therapeutics against generic oral controlled-release drugs. The business models differ: a branded commercial and R&D company against a generic maker and contract manufacturer. The only shared customer type is pharmaceutical wholesalers and distributors, which is too generic to count as a customer overlap.
